platform: Windows, Node 24.18.0, Python 3.14.0, MSYS2 OpenSSH and rsync 3.5.1

reproduction.environmentNotes: Use equivalent local executable and runtime paths. Install the repository dev dependencies for ssh2. SILLYTAVERN_SOURCE is used by the test fixture to resolve yaml; the tests construct their data under .tmp. MSYS2 subprocesses and loopback SSH need an environment that permits them.

wireAuthorizationRetest.note: Retest of one case already counted in the Node suite, with added real daemon filter assertion.

skipReasons: Four Linux flock and SSH entry subprocess cases
One Windows directory symlink privilege case

observations.trafficUnit: rsync protocol bytes; excludes SSH and Tailscale overhead

verified: Deterministic Node and Python bundle bytes, hashes and mtimes, file-size/count/byte group boundaries, and rebuilt corrupted cache
Unsafe or repeated paths, bad bundle digest, invalid binding, oversized bundle, old hello and old job refusal

Full and scoped push and pull using real rsync with production-generated daemon configuration, deletion, empty scope category, scope isolation, path type conversion, stale temporary file cleanup and same-size/same-mtime correction
Rsync wire filter rejects a bundle absent from the frozen descriptors
Real rsync daemon pipe interruption, same-job resume, lost commit acknowledgement after publication and idempotent reconciliation
Lost download finish acknowledgement permits verified staging; explicit finish refusal fails
Real loopback OpenSSH negotiation rejects old peers, changed dataset on reconnect, wrong passwords and changed host keys
Frozen push plan replay after missing bundle and interrupted apply, retained-job checks and bounded reconnect/BUSY behavior
boundaries: Synthetic data under repository .tmp; no production local data, live VPS, Android or deployed installation
Rsync uses a fixture pipe instead of SSH; real loopback OpenSSH exercises authentication, host identity and control negotiation separately
Windows fixture substitutes Linux flock and cp; the updater unit tests do not execute a production update
